id_and_class.summary: Artist Todd Siler approaches consciousness through ‘Metaphorming’: making connections by metaphor, analogy, symbol, model, and story, which he takes to be the creative process of both the human brain and nature. His large NeuroArt paintings picture the brain as connected to everything it creates, and he treats consciousness, with conscience, as what turns organic matter into reflective, creative, empathic beings.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Siler treats consciousness as the source of mind, art, science, and technology, and the condition for reflection, creation, and empathy. He pictures it through Metaphorms, which he holds make up all our symbolic languages and connection-making tools.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Everything humans make is a product of the brain, though how exactly no one knows. Siler coins ‘brainfinity’ for the pairing of a finite brain with an infinite mind.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Consciousness lets humans act with intention instead of drifting ‘like jellyfish adrift without purpose’, and conscience deepens it toward care for others.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: The brain and its synapses; Metaphorms as connection-making devices; nature as possibly one interconnected creative process.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through art-making, intuition, lucid dreaming, and questioning, combined with neuroscience in what Siler calls the ArtScience process.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Synapses as the building blocks that enable curiosity, creativity, imagination, communication, and consciousness.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Metaphorming, the brain's way of connecting anything to something else. Siler also proposes ‘cerebral fusion’: in the Papez circuit of the limbic system, thought, feeling, emotion, and action may merge in milliseconds.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Siler describes a ‘Big Bang of Consciousness’ when humankind began to think, create, and innovate to survive. Mental states vary in alertness and level, and he notes they correlate with the frequency and amplitude of the EEG.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: The brain, with the limbic system's Papez circuit singled out as where affective and cognitive functions may merge.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness makes art, science, technology, and civility possible. Every human problem and every human solution is, for Siler, brain-related.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: His ‘Thought-Assemblies’ work proposes that analytic and artistic thought start from the same insight and converge.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The brain communicates with itself and others in several symbolic languages, which neuroscientists are learning to decode as scholars deciphered the Rosetta Stone.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Siler traces an ascent from molecules to mudskippers to hominids to beings who build both life-sustaining and life-threatening technologies, and asks whether conscience will keep pace.
core_claims_and_evidence: All metaphors, analogies, symbols, numbers, models, and stories are forms of one connection-making process Siler calls Metaphorming.
Creativity is any unconditioned response to familiar or unfamiliar things, and the process may be the same in art, science, and mathematics.
Synapses are the basic building blocks that make thought, feeling, action, and consciousness possible.
Intuition and reason together drive breakthrough thinking and innovation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Artistic practice and personal intuition, informed by neuroscience.

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Siler's own open questions are how the brain connects to everything it creates, how nature connects everything it creates, and how the neural mechanisms of thought shape its contents.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Siler insists that everything human-made is the brain's handiwork, yet he speaks of an infinite mind and of the immaterial (love), and he leaves the tension unresolved.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Siler locates purpose in human creativity, conscience, and love, and in building a more conscientious civilization.
